title: DRC in 2025: Top 10 Flagship Companies
excerpt: From mining giants to public utilities, a look at the ten most influential companies in the Democratic Republic of Congo in 2025.
seo_desc: A panorama of the ten most influential companies in the DRC in 2025, from Gécamines and TFM to Rawbank, SNEL and SNCC, and the challenges they face.
image_alt: Flagship companies of the Democratic Republic of Congo in 2025
body_html:
Kinshasa, 8 December 2025—PRESS AFRICA—Several companies in the Democratic Republic of Congo stand out in 2025 for their economic weight, strategic role and contribution to national development. From mining giants to public utilities, here is an overview of the ten most influential companies in the country.

Gécamines: the Générale des Carrières et des Mines (Gécamines) remains the country's leading state-owned mining company. Founded in Lubumbashi, it is active in the extraction of copper and cobalt, resources that are strategic for the energy transition.

Tenke Fungurume Mining (TFM): a major joint venture in copper and cobalt extraction, TFM is one of the country's biggest producers. It plays a central role in mining development.

Rawbank: the DRC's largest universal bank, Rawbank provides financial services to businesses, SMEs and individuals. It facilitates local investment and plays a key role in Congolese finance.

Bralima: a brewing subsidiary of Heineken, Bralima produces alcoholic and non-alcoholic drinks in several Congolese cities such as Kinshasa, Kisangani and Lubumbashi. Its long history makes it a pillar of local industry.

SNEL (Société Nationale d'Électricité): the state-owned company responsible for the generation, transmission and distribution of electricity in the DRC. In 2025, it is engaged in a vast modernisation and recruitment plan to improve national electricity coverage.

Cohydro: a state-owned hydrocarbons company, Cohydro plays a central role in the import, distribution and trade of fuels across Congolese territory.

MIBA (Société Minière de Bakwanga): a historic player in the DRC's diamond industry, MIBA remains an important company despite structural challenges in the mining sector.

OKIMO (Office des Mines d'Or de Kilo-Moto): a state-owned company specialising in gold, OKIMO holds major concessions in the north-east of the DRC and plays a strategic role in gold mining.

SODIMICO (Société de Développement Industriel et Minier au Congo): a state-owned mining company, SODIMICO is among the Congolese state's holdings in several mining companies.

SNCC (Société Nationale des Chemins de Fer du Congo): a key player in rail transport, SNCC, a state-owned company, plays an essential role in domestic logistics and the transport of mineral resources, a vital link for the national economy.

Outlook…

These ten companies illustrate the diversity of the Congolese economic fabric: a dominant mining sector, but also state-owned companies in energy and transport infrastructure. They represent both levers of development and significant challenges: modernisation, governance and investment capacity.

Governance and transparency: several of these state-owned companies (such as Gécamines, SNEL and OKIMO) face governance challenges. Strengthening transparency and reducing debt are major issues.

Investment in infrastructure: SNEL in particular is carrying out an ambitious project to expand the power grid and bring electricity to rural areas, which could support industrial growth.

Strategic resources: miners such as TFM and Gécamines are at the heart of the global race for strategic metals (copper, cobalt), which gives the DRC a central role in the energy transition.

The DRC's corporate landscape in 2025 is marked by a mix of historic public players, international joint ventures and fast-growing banks. Their collective success is crucial to the country's economic development, and their institutional strengthening could make the Democratic Republic of Congo an even more influential player on the global economic stage.

Writer: BAWA ALLAH Khadidjatou A.
